q.t: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the area of a 90° sector of a circle of radius 14 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: A sector is the fraction θ/360° of the circle: ¼ × 22/7 × 196.

q.t: Find the length of a 60° arc of a circle of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The arc is the fraction 60/360 = 1/6 of the circumference 132.

q.t: Find the area of a circle of diameter 28 cm. (π = 22/7)
A circle has circumference 88 cm. Find its radius. (π = 22/7)
Find the area of a semicircle of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Half of 154.

q.t: Find the area of a quadrant of a circle of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: A quadrant is a quarter: 154/4.

q.t: A wheel has diameter 70 cm. How far does it go in one turn? (π = 22/7)
q.e: One turn rolls out one circumference: π × 70.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a semicircle of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Half the circumference (22) plus the straight diameter (14).

q.t: Find the area of the ring between circles of radii 10.5 cm and 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Big circle minus small circle: π(110.25 − 49).

q.t: Find the area of a 120° sector of a circle of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: 120° is ⅓ of the circle: ⅓ × 1386.

q.t: A minute hand is 14 cm long. What area does it sweep in 5 minutes? (π = 22/7)
q.e: 5 minutes is 30°, i.e. 1/12 of the circle: 616/12.

q.t: A wheel of diameter 84 cm rolls 792 m. How many turns does it make? (π = 22/7)
q.e: Each turn covers π × 84 = 264 cm. 79200 ÷ 264.

q.t: A square is drawn inside a circle of radius 7 cm with its corners on the circle. Find the area inside the circle but outside the square. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The square’s diagonal is the diameter 14, so its area is ½ × 14 × 14 = 98. 154 − 98.

q.t: A circle’s circumference is 30 cm more than its diameter. Find its radius. (π = 22/7)
A circle has circumference 132 cm. Find its area. (π = 22/7)
Find the perimeter of a 60° sector of a circle of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Arc 22 plus two radii 42.

q.t: A chord of a circle of radius 21 cm makes a right angle at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Segment = sector − triangle: ¼ × 1386 − ½ × 21 × 21 = 346.5 − 220.5.

q.t: A horse is tied with a 14 m rope to a corner of a large rectangular field. How much area can it graze? (π = 22/7)
q.e: The corner is a right angle, so it can reach a quadrant: ¼ × 616.

q.t: A chord of a circle of radius 21 cm makes 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Sector = 1/6 × 1386 = 231. The triangle is equilateral (two radii, 60° between), area (√3/4) × 441.

q.t: A square of side 14 cm has a quadrant of radius 7 cm cut from each corner. Find the area left. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Four quarter-circles make one full circle of area 154. 196 − 154.

q.t: A circle’s area equals the sum of the areas of circles with radii 6 cm and 8 cm. Find its radius.
A circle’s circumference equals the sum of the circumferences of circles with radii 15 cm and 11 cm. Find its radius.
A car’s wheels have diameter 70 cm. How many turns does each wheel make per minute at 66 km/h? (π = 22/7)
q.e: 66 km/h = 1100 m per minute = 110000 cm. Each turn is 220 cm.

q.t: An equilateral triangle of side 14 cm has a circle of radius 7 cm drawn at each corner. Find the area of the triangle not covered by the circles. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Triangle = (√3/4) × 196 = 49√3. Each corner holds a 60° sector; three of them make half a circle: 77.

q.t: Find the area of the largest circle that can be cut from a 20 cm × 14 cm rectangle. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Its diameter cannot exceed the shorter side, 14 cm.

q.t: A clock’s hour hand is 7 cm long. What area does it sweep from 9 a.m. to 12 noon? (π = 22/7)
q.e: 3 hours is 3/12 of a full turn = 90°: ¼ × 154.

q.t: Two circles have areas in the ratio 4 : 9. Find the ratio of their circumferences.
q.e: Area ratio is the square of the radius ratio, so radii are 2 : 3 — and circumference goes with the radius.

q.t: A sector of a circle of radius 7 cm has perimeter 25 cm. Find its angle in degrees. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The arc is 25 − 14 = 11, which is 11/44 = ¼ of the circumference.

q.t: A car has two wipers 14 cm long that do not overlap. Each sweeps 135°. Find the total area cleaned. (π = 22/7)
A circular brooch of radius 7 cm is divided into 8 equal sectors by 4 diameters. Find the area of each sector. (π = 22/7)
A chord of a circle of radius 20 cm makes a right angle at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (π = 3.14)
q.e: Minor segment = 314 − 200 = 114. Major = whole circle 1256 − 114.

q.t: Four semicircles are drawn inward on the sides of a 14 cm square, making a four-petal flower. Find the area of the flower. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The four semicircles (77 each) cover the square and overlap exactly on the petals: 308 − 196.

q.t: A running track has two straight 100 m parts and semicircular ends. The inner ends have diameter 56 m and the track is 7 m wide. Find its area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Straights 2 × 100 × 7 = 1400. Two semicircular rings make one full ring between radii 28 and 35: 22/7 × 441 = 1386.

q.t: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm makes 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Sector = 1/6 × 616 = 308/3. The triangle is equilateral of side 14: (√3/4) × 196 = 49√3.

q.t: A 21 cm pendulum swings through 36°. Find the length of the arc its tip moves along. (π = 22/7)
Three circles of radius 3.5 cm each touch the other two. Find the area enclosed between them. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The centres form an equilateral triangle of side 7. Its three 60° corner sectors make half a circle: ½ × 38.5.

q.t: A ring has area 462 cm² and outer radius 14 cm. Find the inner radius. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Inner circle area = 616 − 462 = 154, so r² = 49.

q.t: A circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side 12√3 cm. Find its area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The incircle radius is side ÷ (2√3) = 6 (one-third of the height 18). 22/7 × 36.
